Reddit announced two upcoming changes that some long-time users may not be happy about.

The company has already placed one restriction on old Reddit, and now a second has been revealed. Additionally, RSS support is going away...

Old Reddit

Reddit overhauled its user interface significantly in 2018, which was met with strong backlash from users who preferred the original layout. In response to this feedback, the platform said it would keep the old interface, colloquially known as "old Reddit," as long as users continued to use it.

The first policy change came in August of this year, when the company required users on old Reddit to be logged in. Now, the company is announcing that the original interface will only be available to users who have used it within the last six months, with new users being locked out.

Reddit says both of these measures are intended to reduce AI scraping on the platform (although that sort of activity seems to be fine if a company is willing to pay).

RSS Feeds Going Away

Disabling RSS feeds was explained using the same reasoning.

This change may be particularly disruptive for subreddits that rely on RSS to handle their moderation workflows. Reddit says it is aware of this and suggests that moderators use Devvit apps, such as Discord Relay.

Users Aren't Happy

A glance at the comments section makes it clear that many long-time users are quite unhappy with these latest developments.

What are your thoughts on these latest changes? Share them in the comments.
